name: Flesh Pink
lede: Flesh Pink is a pale pinkish beige, a name from the old habit of describing colors by skin.

sections.title: From skin to stockings
sections.body:
Paterson traces flesh-colour to the 1920s, when pink silk stockings were given the name; hence flesh-tint and flesh-toned, which describes pinkish shades like the human complexion [1]. Flesh-red, a related term, is used for minerals and crystals [1].

Gage reproduces a Renaissance list of pleasing color combinations that includes green with red or flesh-pink [2]. He also notes the composer Scriabin gave some musical keys a flesh-pink with a glint of steel in his colored-light scheme [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: #F0C2B8 sits near [[peach]] and [[salmon]] in the screen data [9]. Paterson's dictionary also lists plain flesh as a moderate pink, which fits a pale, warm swatch like this one [1]. These are as-seen screen colors, not skin measurements [1]. The concordance of 29 color books finds only four strong mentions of this name, so the article stays short rather than pad the record [9]. Screen colors are approximate, and the swatch is a reference value, not a measured pigment [9].
